record.paper_title: Offline Reinforcement Learning: Tutorial, Review, and Perspectives on Open Problems
record.context_brief: Function-approximation error accumulation in offline dynamic programming
record.original_question: How can offline dynamic-programming algorithms with neural-network value functions prevent brittle function-approximation errors, small-dataset overfitting, and accumulated Bellman-backup errors when there is no online data collection to provide corrective feedback?

evidence.quote: Even when the behavior policy can be estimated exactly, a number of these methods still suffer from the undesirable effects of function approximation. When neural networks are used to represent Q-functions, undesirable effects of function approximation may prevent the Q-function from learning meaningful values even when out-of-distribution actions are controlled for in the target values. For example, when the size of the dataset is limited, approximate dynamic programming algorithms tend to overfit on the small dataset, and this error is then accumulated via Bellman backups (Fu et al., 2019; Kumar et al., 2020a).

Unlike online reinforcement learning, where accidental overestimation errors arising due to function approximation can be corrected via active data collection, these errors cumulatively build up and affect future iterates in an offline RL setting.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a Markov decision process with state space $\mathcal{S}$, action space $\mathcal{A}$, transition kernel $P(s'\mid s,a)$, reward function $r(s,a)$, and discount factor $\gamma \in [0,1)$. In the offline (batch) reinforcement learning setting, the learner is given a fixed dataset $\mathcal{D} = \{(s_i, a_i, r_i, s_i')\}_{i=1}^N$ generated by some unknown behavior policy $\pi_\beta$, and is not permitted to interact further with the environment. Approximate dynamic programming methods seek a parametric action-value function $Q_\theta : \mathcal{S}\times\mathcal{A}\to\mathbb{R}$ (typically a neural network) by iterating an approximate Bellman backup
$$Q_{\theta_{k+1}} \leftarrow \arg\min_{Q_\theta} \mathbb{E}_{(s,a,s')\sim\mathcal{D}}\Big[\big(Q_\theta(s,a) - r(s,a) - \gamma\, \mathbb{E}_{a'\sim\pi(\cdot\mid s')}[Q_{\theta_k}(s',a')]\big)^2\Big].$$
In this setting, even when the behavior policy is known exactly and out-of-distribution actions are explicitly excluded from target computations, function-approximation errors can still arise from (i) overfitting of $Q_\theta$ to the finite dataset $\mathcal{D}$, (ii) extrapolation errors of the neural network on under-supported regions of $\mathcal{S}\times\mathcal{A}$, and (iii) accumulation of these errors across successive Bellman backups, since no further data may be collected to correct them.

Problem: Design an offline approximate dynamic-programming algorithm using neural network value functions, together with a theoretical analysis, that provably controls and prevents the cumulative growth of function-approximation error across Bellman iterations. Specifically, give an algorithm and finite-sample bound establishing that the suboptimality $\|Q^{\pi^*} - Q_{\theta_K}\|$ (in an appropriate norm) of the resulting policy after $K$ iterations remains bounded, with explicit dependence on $N$, $K$, $\gamma$, and the capacity of the function class, that does not blow up due to error accumulation, and that does not require any additional online data collection.
artifact.status_search_result: This is a broad open challenge in offline reinforcement learning. While many algorithmic approaches (e.g., conservative Q-learning, BCQ, IQL, behavior-regularized actor-critic) have been proposed and partially mitigate error accumulation under coverage assumptions, no single method provably eliminates brittle function-approximation errors and accumulated Bellman-backup errors in full generality with neural networks. The problem remains an active research area.

status_evidence.title: Offline Reinforcement Learning: Tutorial, Review, and Perspectives on Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Identifies function-approximation error accumulation as an open problem in offline RL.
status_evidence.claim: The problem of preventing accumulated function-approximation error in offline dynamic programming is identified as open.
